doc.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Presenting film shows and the size of the collection
summary: Wolff discusses balancing talk with film in presentations and says he does not count his collection, which he shares with other collectors.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: It’s so interesting to watch the audience at your little presentations there, and we see a face and you say now who is that? And people just love to zero in on these personalities.

Well you know you’re torn when you put these shows on. Do you want to continuously talk through the movie, or do you want to let the people enjoy the films? And I have always chosen the latter of those two courses, the most consistent criticism I get is that I should talk more often. I think that’s a better criticism than you talk too much.
Right. Because when you know these little great anecdotes about people, you constantly want to say, “Now this fella here—” and it’s very hard not to talk.

If I could just make the films shorter and leave more time for talking when the films weren’t being shown, I might be able to reach a balance. But what happens is if I get an hour to do a film, like I had for yesterday, the film was an hour and thirteen minutes long. I didn’t know what to cut.
Well you’ve amassed quite a collection of films. How many, do you have a number of films that you have now?

No. No more than I have a number of 33s that I have. I think when you collect you don’t want to get into numbers. I don’t put a dollar value on it, I have no idea how much I have. What I do know is that it is one of the largest in the world and I share with people all over the world, other collectors. And I’m kind of proud to say that I feel the collection is there to be shared not to be hoarded and not to be kept private, so it is something that I’ve really enjoyed and that I like to think I help other people enjoy as well.
